title: 1. Sources of Information About Earth's Interior

blocks.content: The study of the behavior of seismic waves is the most important source of information about the interior of the earth.

rows: Deep Ocean Drilling Projects & Kola Borehole (12 km)
Volcanic eruptions throwing magma to the surface
Mining samples (e.g., 3-4 km deep South African gold mines)
Gravity anomalies, magnetic surveys, and pressure-temperature gradients

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Direct sources of information about Earth's interior include surface rocks, deep mining, ocean drilling projects, and volcanic material.
Indirect sources include the analysis of temperature and pressure increases with depth, density changes, meteors, gravitation, magnetic fields, and seismic activity.
Seismic waves are categorized into body waves (P-waves and S-waves) and surface waves; P-waves travel through all mediums while S-waves travel only through solids.
The existence of seismic shadow zones helps scientists map the boundaries and liquid nature of Earth's outer core.
S-waves cannot pass through liquids; this property proved that Earth's outer core is liquid.
Gravity anomaly refers to the difference between the observed value of gravity and the expected theoretical value, indicating mass distribution in the crust.
The deepest ocean drilling project is at Kola in the Arctic Ocean, reaching a depth of 12 km.
